page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-16 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine instance within the Standard E5 family. It is driven by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 4 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, presenting 8 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated hardware accelerators or local NVMe storage, meaning that storage operations rely exclusively on external network-attached volumes. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware footprint maintains a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system offers cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing compute throughput over expansive memory footprints, reducing the overhead of unneeded memory capacity.

This hardware balance is best suited for compute-intensive tasks with moderate working memory requirements. Typical deployment targets include web application serving, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch compute processes, and distributed compute worker nodes.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-16 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 2 threads per core, providing 8 vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio designed for compute-centric workloads that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. The configuration features no local disk storage and contains no discrete graphics hardware, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. VM.Standard.E5.Flex.4-16 is suited for web serving, microservices, batch processing, and CI/CD pipelines.
